items.title: Re Riemann
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
🫧 Open on Bubbles

And I see this mural, and think: how great is Man! Our life is like a breath of air, we were beset by illness and hunger and cold, millions and hundreds of millions died in plagues. And yet we—sick, hungry, short-lived—learned the system of the world, crawled out of the caves, brought nature to heel, walked on the Moon. The last shall be first! And eyes that are clouded with age have seen the furthest stars, and the lives of a cell, and the worlds of Cantor and Hilbert: the invisible world that waited forever. We are dust and ashes, and yet our minds bestride the universe. How great is Man!

And when I read the Riemann announcement, when I read Machines of Loving Grace : humanity is not at the center. Claude is at the center. We are hidden in the margins, passive recipients of manna from Claude. How great is Claude! How noble in reason, how infinite in benevolence! The dancing star, the living word !

Fernando Borretti

items.title: “The Bluet” by James Schuyler
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
And is it stamina

that unseasonably freaks

forth a bluet, a

Quaker lady, by

the lake? So small,

a drop of sky that

splashed and held,

four-petaled, creamy

in its throat. The woods

around were brown,

the air crisp as a

Carr's table water

biscuit and smelt of

cider. There were frost

apples on the trees in

the field below the house.

The pond was still, then

broke into a ripple.

The hills, the leaves that

have not yet fallen

are deep and oriental

rug colors. Brown leaves

in the woods set off

gray trunks of trees.

But that bluet was

the focus of it all: last

spring, next spring, what

does it matter? Unexpected

as a tear when someone

reads a poem you wrote

for him: "It's this line

here." That bluet breaks

me up, tiny spring flower

late, late in dour October.

items.title: I tried to listen to music
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
Sometimes online, I stumble upon posts of people born before music streaming was a thing and they explain how listening to new music back then was an experience.

They would go to the shop, buy a CD or vinyl after struggling to choose. Then they'd come home, and listen to the music they had just bought. Nothing more, simply sitting there and listening.

This is really foreign to me as I've always seen music as a commodity. Music is the thing you put in the car, while washing the dishes, when you have a long walk to go somewhere, what's on at the radio when you're grocery shopping.

It is never about the music itself, more like an enjoyable background noise that you pay some attention to, but never all your attention.

And it makes sense that it works that way for me, because music has always been so easily available in nearly infinite quantities so it seems like a nice but unimportant thing.

I had spent MONTHS trying to figure out what I wanted to talk about.

I’ve been programming since 2004, building iOS apps since 2010, and giving technical talks for years. I’ve worked on fastlane, spent years helping developers ship software, organized Deep Dish Swift, and given more technical talks than I can probably remember.

But none of those ideas excited me. The more I tried to force myself into one of those topics, the more I realized that none of them felt particularly honest about the year I’d just had.

And apparently it took me several months and a ridiculous number of slide revisions to figure that out. 😅

For most of my career, I’ve had a pretty interesting relationship with productivity.

My nonverbal ASD diagnosed son is not being given access to the communication device listed in his IEP at least some of the time and I don't know what I can do about it. I need advice on how to be That Parent.

Tiny Monster is non-verbal and uses an AAC (a locked down iPad Mini that runs only his communication program). He's by no means conversational but he has some proficiency with it. I must stress that this is a device that was prescribed by his speech therapist, paid for by our health insurance, not a personal entertainment device.

I went to an event at his school today and afterwards went with him to his classroom to get his stuff. You struck a deal with a dragon: twenty years of protection for twenty years of dinner service. The island thrives under the beast's watchful eye, as long as the meals keep coming.
